answer: Tiered collateral floors that rise with influence resist sybils: an identity posts more collateral to UNLOCK each higher tier of power, so accumulating real influence across fakes needs proportionally more locked capital per head. A shale-thin bond buys only the lowest tier; climbing to the ivory heights of full influence demands escalating collateral per identity. An honest agent funds one climb; an attacker who wants his fleet to MATTER funds the rising floor for every fake, so a farm that wanders toward power pays a steeply increasing bill.
